Letters of encouragement

Write a few lines that warm someone’s heart

A handwritten note, slipped into an outreach bag or handed over during a visit, is often kept for years. The team will read your letter, then deliver it by hand.

To keep everyone safe

  1. Letters are always delivered by the team: no direct contact, especially with children.
  2. Do not include your last name, address, phone number or social media in the letter.
  3. No money, gifts or promises: just words.
  4. The team may remove a passage, or not deliver a letter that doesn’t follow these rules.
  5. The people who receive a letter only know your first name (or “a friend”).

Not sure what to write?

  • Tell them one simple thing that made you smile this week.
  • Share a verse that carried you through a hard time.
  • Say what you wish for them this coming winter.
  • Write a prayer for them, in your own words.
